data.title: Berkshire Hathaway Q2 earnings on deck; look for buybacks, cash, float
data.description:
Following Warren Buffett's long tradition, Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) (BRK.A), now helmed by Greg Abel, is set to post Q2 results on Saturday at 7:00 AM Central Time (8:00 AM ET).

The Omaha, Nebraska-based investing behemoth is expected to report Q2 operating earnings of $10.8B, according to the consensus estimate, up from $10.2B in Q1. 

Investors, though, will also be focused on the company's cash and Treasury holdings, which have continued to pile up for years. At March 31, 2026, it stood at $397.4B.

Steve Check, president and chief investment officer of Check Capital Management, which holds ~$500M of Berkshire stock and ~$600M in Berkshire options, wants to see the company use more of its cash holdings for stock buybacks.

"Stock buybacks are the most natural use of the cash if the stock is priced right," he told Seeking Alpha in an interview. Buying back about $50B of stock per year would likely keep Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.B) (BRK.A) cash holdings about even, he figures. 

He was a “little disappointed” in the ~$234M of stock the company repurchased in the first quarter of the year. Check expects that to change. "My understanding is that, when we get the quarterly numbers, we're going to find out the buyback was quite significant" in Q2, he said.

Investors have curbed their expectations of using the cash hoard for any “elephant-sized” acquisitions. Buffett, who remains chairman of Berkshire, is well known for his discipline in not buying when asset valuations are rich. In  prior years, he has made plain his preference to acquire stakes in well-run publicly traded companies, rather than buy entire companies outright.

After Q2 ended, Berkshire (BRK.B) closed on what's considered a relatively small acquisition — the $6.8B purchase of homebuilder Taylor Morrison Homes.

When it comes to Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.A) (BRK.B) operations, Check will be looking at insurance, especially the underwriting side. While the company owns a sprawling range of businesses, "insurance is certainly the engine of Berkshire," he said. Underwriting is expected to be a bit tougher this quarter, he said. "It's a bit softer market."

Q2 insurance underwriting income is expected to be $2.05B, according to the Visible Alpha consensus. That's up from. $1.72B in the prior quarter but down 19% from Q2 2025.

Check will also be looking at its insurance float, which stood at $176.9B at the end of Q1. If the company makes 4.4% on that, that's a significant number for what is essentially “free” money, he said.

For the overall operations, the money manager expects results to be "flat to up" on most subsidiaries. But neither is Check expecting blockbuster performance from the company. He calls the company a "good cornerstone… a very steady 8%-10% grower." In the past year, Berkshire B shares rose ~13%, lagging the S&P 500's 22% increase.

As for Abel's performance at the company, "it's pretty early on," Check said. Still, he's happy with the choice of Buffett's successor. "We couldn't ask for a better choice," he said. 

"I don't think Greg Abel is going to do anything dumb. He might be a little bit on the conservative side, but so is Warren Buffett, for that matter," Check said.

data.title: Post declines after third-quarter results
data.description:
Post Holdings (POST) shares declined over 12% on Friday as investors were disappointed with the company’s weaker-than-expected third quarter revenue.

The consumer packaged goods holding company reported Q3 revenue of $1.9B, missing consensus by $130M. Adjusted diluted earnings per common share were $1.78, compared to $2.03 in the prior year period.

The company said sales and profit for primarily egg and potato products saw a decline, reflecting the lapping of avian influenza pricing in the prior year period.

Looking forward, Post narrowed its guidance range for fiscal year 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $1,560-$1,570 million from $1,550-$1,580 million.

The stock was trading at $78.63 in morning trading on Friday. Overall, it has lost 20% so far this year, compared to the nearly 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

Seeking Alpha and Wall Street analysts are bullish and rated the stock a Buy and above, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant ratings consider it a Hold.

data.title: Sega Sammy Holdings reports Q1 results
Corsair Gaming jumps 34% as record margins, higher guidance fuel rally
data.description:
Corsair Gaming (CRSR) stock soared more than 34% on Friday after the gaming hardware maker reported stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 earnings, driven by record margins, higher profitability, and an improved full-year outlook.

The stock is up about 139% year to date, outperforming the S&P 500 Index (SP500), which has gained 12.6%.

The company reported non-GAAP EPS of $0.23, beating estimates by $0.16, while revenue of $314.3M topped expectations by $3.9M, despite slipping 2% YoY.

The biggest positive was profitability. Gross margin expanded to a record 33.2%, while gross profit rose 21% to $104.3M. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 279% to $30.8M, far above the company's guidance, and Corsair Gaming swung to GAAP net income of $9.1M from a $20.3M loss a year earlier.

Investors also welcomed the company's higher 2026 guidance, with management expecting revenue of $1.40B-$1.47B, adjusted EBITDA of $121M-$131M, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.85-$0.94.

For the third quarter, the company forecasts revenue of $320M-$350M, adjusted EBITDA of $18M-$21M, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.09-$0.12.

Strong demand for Fanatec, Elgato, and Stream Deck products helped drive growth in the Gamer and Creator Peripherals segment, while the recent acquisition of Trak Racer further strengthens the company's sim racing business.

Following the rally, the stock has a Hold rating from Seeking Alpha analysts, while Wall Street and Quant maintain Buy ratings.

data.title: Immigration crackdown fails to lift native-born employment
data.description:
The employment rate for prime-age native-born Americans fell to its lowest level in more than four years, despite the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, economist Joey Politano said, citing the latest U.S. labor market data.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls declined by 23K in July, missing the +88K consensus and erasing the 20K increase in June, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday.

Politano said a key economic argument behind the administration's mass deportation policy had been that reducing immigration would create more jobs for native-born Americans. He said the latest data did not support that outcome.

A chart shared by Politano showed the 12-month moving average employment rate for native-born Americans aged 25 to 54 trending lower recently, while the employment rate for foreign-born workers remained broadly flat.

The chart also showed both employment rates recovering from their pandemic-era lows before leveling off over the past few years. The employment rate for native-born workers remained above that of foreign-born workers throughout the period shown.

Politano said the latest figures challenged the view that fewer immigrants would necessarily translate into stronger employment outcomes for native-born Americans.

data.title: Yelp targets $250M other revenue run rate by end of 2028 while guiding Q3 revenue to $365M-$370M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Yelp (YELP) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "Yelp continued to advance its AI transformation in the second quarter," said (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Jeremy Stoppelman), adding that the company "expanded the reach of our trusted content through new partnerships" and saw "meaningful signs of improvement that emerge across several key metrics," while noting "consumers and local businesses have continued to face a challenging economic environment."

  • (CEO Stoppelman) tied the quarter’s mix shift to AI-led initiatives: "We've increased our focus on growing a number of AI-driven revenue streams this year," and said that "Other revenue growth accelerating from the first quarter to 98% year-over-year" was supported by those efforts; he also pointed to consumer trends, saying, "we saw encouraging traffic trends in the quarter with improvements in app installs and page views."

  • (CEO Stoppelman) emphasized product-led monetization in Services: "the new Yelp Assistant, which works across all categories, demonstrated early positive signs in user engagement" and "contributing to overall project growth of approximately 10% year-over-year."

  • (CEO Stoppelman) highlighted scaling in restaurants and platform distribution: "Yelp Host... reached an annual run rate of 2.4 million calls handled in July," and he said Yelp added "an integration with OpenTable" plus "food ordering functionality with full point-of-sale integration"; he also described licensing momentum, saying, "Yelp ratings and reviews recently began powering ChatGPT's local experience in relevant categories" and "Request-a-Quote integration with ChatGPT is coming soon."

  • "Net revenue increased by 1% year-over-year to $376 million, $8 million above the high end of our outlook range," said (Chief Financial Officer David Schwarzbach), and added: "We have now paused our [share repurchase] program as we work to pay down our revolving credit facility... we expect to resume repurchases in 2027."

Outlook

  • "We anticipate third quarter net revenue will be in the range of $365 million to $370 million," said (CFO Schwarzbach), while warning, "we anticipate that the challenging economic environment for local businesses will persist for the remainder of the year and continue impacting advertising revenue across categories."

  • "For the full year, we are narrowing our range and now expect net revenue will be between $1.460 billion and $1.470 billion," said (CFO Schwarzbach), and: "For the full year, we are narrowing our range and now expect adjusted EBITDA will be between $315 million and $325 million."

  • (CFO Schwarzbach) described near-term margin pressure from investment: "we expect expenses will increase sequentially in the third quarter as we invest in our AI transformation, Hatch, and consumer marketing" and guided that "third quarter adjusted EBITDA will be in the range of $70 million to $75 million."

Financial results

  • Yelp reported $376 million of net revenue, $32 million of net income (8% margin), and $91 million of adjusted EBITDA (24% margin) for Q2 2026, according to (CFO Schwarzbach).

  • (CFO Schwarzbach) detailed ad-category performance and advertiser activity: "Services ad revenue was flat year-over-year at $241 million, while RR&O ad revenue decreased by 10% year-over-year to $102 million," and "paying advertising locations" declined "1% year-over-year... to 510,000" alongside "Ad clicks" down "5% year-over-year" and "Average CPC" up "1%."

  • (CFO Schwarzbach) attributed the fastest-growing line to new businesses and licensing: "Other revenue increased by 98% year-over-year to a record $33 million" driven by "the inclusion of revenue generated by Hatch" plus "significant growth in revenue from data licensing and food ordering."

  • (CFO Schwarzbach) set a longer-term milestone for the newer streams: "we are targeting an annual run rate of $250 million in Other revenue by the end of 2028."

Q&A

  • Alex (for Eric Sheridan), Goldman Sachs: asked about Hatch investment areas and long-term margin structure; (CFO Schwarzbach) said, "We are investing in Hatch... both in go-to-market as well as product and engineering" and that longer-term margin profile "can be similar to other subscription businesses," while adding, "In the near term... we definitely want to continue to invest to scale."

  • Sergio Segura, KeyBanc: asked how Yelp captures economic value from AI (traffic vs. licensing vs. leads); (CEO Stoppelman) said OpenAI is "still kind of the first inning," noted ChatGPT includes "ratings" and "review snippets" that "link back to Yelp," and called it "a potentially significant distribution channel over time"; on lead quality, he added, "it's quite early to really have a strong opinion on that" and "I really haven't seen any data on conversions."

  • Zachary Witaszek (for Colin Sebastian), Baird: asked about cross-selling ads with Yelp Host and partnerships; (CEO Stoppelman) said Host is at "a 2.4 million call run rate" and described OpenTable and food-ordering additions; on ads, he said, "we do see some positive synergies there" but "it's early days" and "I don't think it's really changed the game for us on the restaurant ad side."

  • Nitin Bansal, BofA: asked why paid-search lead acquisition may work now and asked about PAL trends vs. revenue-guide adjustment; (Chief Operating Officer Joseph Nachman) said the difference is "we're specifically targeting multi-location Services businesses" and added, "we're really confident in the ROAS of that spend"; on PALs, he said "Overall, PALs were down 1% year-over-year, which is a big improvement over Q1," while cautioning, "we don't expect any massive trajectory turn" given "macroeconomic pressures."

  • Kishan Patel (for Josh Beck), Raymond James: asked about Google traffic tailwinds vs. AI overview headwinds and paid vs. organic; (CEO Stoppelman) said, "it does seem that we've bucked the trend" and described Yelp as "largely... organically driven," adding that paid traffic is "relatively de minimis in terms of overall traffic impact."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to pressing, focusing on monetization durability (AI distribution value capture, lead quality), advertising/location trends versus guidance, and whether new investments change margin structure.

  • Management sentiment was slightly positive in prepared remarks ("We are confident in our plans for the year") and more cautious in Q&A when data was early ("it's quite early"; "I really haven't seen any data on conversions") and when discussing macro ("challenging economic environment").

  • Versus last quarter, management continued to emphasize AI transformation and other revenue, but Q2 included more explicit caution around near-term investment ("expenses will increase sequentially") and a capital-return shift (pausing repurchases to pay down the revolver).

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 introduced a formal pause in repurchases and a stated plan to "resume repurchases in 2027," whereas Q1 emphasized ongoing 2026 repurchases.

  • The AI/product narrative remained consistent across quarters (Yelp Assistant, Host, Hatch, licensing), but Q2 added distribution detail that "Yelp ratings and reviews... began powering ChatGPT's local experience" and that a "Request-a-Quote integration with ChatGPT is coming soon."

  • Guidance language tightened in Q2: management said it was "narrowing" full-year net revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges, while continuing to cite a "challenging economic environment" affecting advertising.

Risks and concerns

  • (CEO Stoppelman) said "consumers and local businesses have continued to face a challenging economic environment," and (CFO Schwarzbach) said it will "persist for the remainder of the year" and "continue impacting advertising revenue across categories."

  • Integration and scaling risk was acknowledged in Hatch: (CEO Stoppelman) said expanding the team created "an adjustment period in the quarter," though he added "we saw improved trends in July."

  • Measurement uncertainty on AI-platform leads remained open: (CEO Stoppelman) said on AI-platform lead conversion, "it's quite early" and he had not seen conversion data yet.

Final takeaway

Management presented Q2 as continued execution on an AI-led shift toward higher-growth “Other revenue” streams (Hatch, Yelp Host, and licensing) alongside pressured ad categories in a “challenging economic environment.” Leadership guided to sequentially higher investment in Q3, narrowed full-year ranges, highlighted a $250 million Other revenue run-rate target by end of 2028, and described pausing share repurchases to prioritize paying down the revolving credit facility, while positioning ChatGPT distribution and an upcoming Request-a-Quote integration as incremental reach for Services over time.

data.title: The Joint reiterates 2026 outlook while cutting new clinic openings to 22-26
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: The Joint Corp. (JYNT) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "The second quarter was a period of continued execution of our Joint 2.0 initiative, with our results reflecting the progress we are making toward a stronger, more profitable financial profile as a capital-light, pure-play franchisor," said CEO, President & Director Sanjiv Razdan. "This was underscored by a $560,000 year-over-year improvement in consolidated net income and a $1.4 million increase in adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations."

  • "We delivered 152% year-over-year growth in cash flow from operating activities, resulting in a $1.6 million increase in free cash flow," Razdan said, adding that the drivers included "continued progress on our refranchising initiative," "disciplined capital allocation," and "significant improvement in our patient retention levels."

  • On refranchising status, Razdan said, "Since entering into the sale agreement covering the Southern California clinic bundle, ownership has been transferred for 32 clinics to date, and the remaining 13 clinics are being operated by the buyer under management service agreements," and "for the Southeast bundle, ownership has been transferred for 6 clinics to date, with the remaining 15 clinics also operating under management service agreements." He added, "Once ownership transfers are finalized across these clinic bundles, we will have only 3 remaining company-owned or managed clinics."

  • On pricing and membership strategy, Razdan said, "In July, we rolled out our $5 and $10 pricing increases to additional clinics, bringing the total number of clinics that have opted to take pricing to over 500," and "feedback to date continues to indicate no meaningful patient pushback." He also said Q2 patient retention was "our best quarterly retention rate in over 5 years" due to "new flexible and expanded plan options introduced earlier this year."

  • "Revenue grew 14% to $15.2 million," said CFO Scott Bowman. "Selling and marketing expenses were $4.9 million, an increase of 40%... driven by a shift in local marketing to national marketing," and "included in G&A expenses is approximately $500,000 that relates to expenses incurred for RD buybacks and expenses that will not be recurring post-refranchising."

Outlook

  • "We are reiterating our full year 2026 financial guidance as originally provided in March 2026," Bowman said. "We continue to expect system-wide sales of from $519 million to $552 million, comp sales in the range of negative 3% to positive 3%, consolidated adjusted EBITDA in the range of $12.5 million to $13.5 million."

  • On cadence, Bowman said, "We expect comp sales to improve in the second half of the year, with the fourth quarter expected to be higher than the third quarter."

  • On development, Bowman said, "We have more visibility on new franchise clinic openings for the year, which we now expect to be in the range of 22 to 26. This compares to prior guidance of 30 to 35 new clinics," and he added, "on a net basis, our clinic count at the end of the 2026 year will be lower than 2025."

Financial Results

  • "System-wide sales in the second quarter were $128 million, a decline of 3.7%," Bowman said, and "comp sales were negative 2.8%, a 140 basis point improvement from the first quarter."

  • "Revenue grew 14% to $15.2 million," Bowman said, while "cost of revenues was $2.5 million, down 11%." He also reported "net loss from continuing operations was $251,000" and "consolidated net income was $653,000."

  • On cash and capital allocation, Bowman said, "Unrestricted cash at the end of the second quarter was $22.2 million," and the company’s "$20 million line of credit with JPMorgan Chase... remains fully undrawn and is available through August 2029." He added, "we repurchased approximately 82,000 shares for consideration of $677,000 at an average price of $8.23 per share," with "$3.8 million remaining" under the authorization.

  • On the post-refranchising model, Bowman said the “starting points” include "gross margin between 83% and 85% of revenues" and "free cash flow conversion... between 60% and 70%," resulting in "estimated adjusted EBITDA margin of 19% to 21% and net income margin of 13% to 15%."

Q&A

  • Nicholas Sherwood, Maxim Group: "How are you operating in this new AI search environment" to drive click-through? CEO Razdan: "the AI search environment is just incredibly rapidly changing," and the company relies on local franchisee feedback, a digital team tracking "algorithm changes," and "a measurement system"; "our AI score... was in the low 70s, 71 to be precise" and "for the last several months now, we have been in the high 70s."

  • Sherwood, Maxim Group: What drives lapsed patients and how do you win them back? CEO Razdan: "pain, time, money, the 3 biggest drivers," and "our August promotion right now is targeted towards them" to bring them back "at a lower cost of acquisition over time." CFO Bowman: "With this Align One plan... you pay $35, you get 1 visit per month" and "our conversion rate for those lapsed patients has gone up several hundred basis points."

  • George Kelly, ROTH: Provide comp trends (including July) and quantify pricing benefit. CFO Bowman: comps were "a little bit better" late in Q2 and "July comps are a bit better than closing out Q2"; pricing was "helping in the low single-digit range" and could be "at the high end of that low single-digit range" in 2H. CEO Razdan: "we've been doing is taking pricing only for new patients."

  • Kelly, ROTH: What drives further margin improvement beyond the pro forma model, and can you guide to 2027-2028? CFO Bowman: "We're not ready to guide to '27 and '28," and said the deck model "is a starting point" where incremental sales can "leverage" the cost structure; "about $0.5 million in the quarter will not recur."

  • Kelly, ROTH: Timing and remaining proceeds from clinics not yet transferred. CFO Bowman: ownership transfers depend on "lease assignments" and remaining proceeds "it'll be a little bit less of $500,000 or maybe a little less."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts slightly negative to neutral, focused on execution details and proof points on comps, pricing lift, AI search disruption, and the sustainability of the post-refranchising margin framework (e.g., "any comment on July would be helpful" and "how should we think about '27 and '28?").

  • Management slightly positive in prepared remarks and more detailed but measured in Q&A, emphasizing improving trends and reiterating guidance, while using caution on longer-dated targets (e.g., CFO Bowman: "We're not ready to guide to '27 and '28").

  • Versus Q1, the tone shifted toward operational follow-through on refranchising mechanics and near-term sales drivers (Q2 discussion of "lease assignments" and July comps), while Q1 placed more emphasis on refranchising milestones and earlier-stage Joint 3.0 positioning.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q2 kept the same full-year ranges for system-wide sales, comp sales, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA, while development expectations tightened: Q2 guided "22 to 26" new franchise clinic openings "compares to prior guidance of 30 to 35 new clinics" from Q1.

  • Q2 refranchising detail moved from “signed”/“pending closing” in Q1 to active transfer execution, including clinics operating "under management service agreements" in multiple bundles and a comment that remaining proceeds are "a little bit less of $500,000 or maybe a little less."

  • Analyst focus shifted from Q1’s timing to close refranchising and price elasticity to Q2’s comp trajectory into July, quantified pricing contribution, and clarifying the “starting point” nature of the pro forma margin slide.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Comp sales were negative 2.8%" in Q2 and "system-wide sales... a decline of 3.7%," with management tying recovery expectations to retention, marketing, pricing rollout, and winning back lapsed patients.

  • Refranchising completion risk remained tied to third-party lease work: Bowman said the process is "rather lengthy" because the company "ha[s] to work with the landlords to execute the lease assignments."

  • Expense normalization and execution risk were highlighted by one-time items: Bowman said "approximately $500,000" in G&A was related to RD buybacks and refranchising items "that will not be recurring post-refranchising."

Final Takeaway

Management positioned Q2 as continued progress toward a capital-light, pure-play franchisor model, citing improved profitability and cash generation alongside “best” retention in over five years and expanded pricing adoption to over 500 clinics. The company reiterated its 2026 system-wide sales, comp, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA outlook, while reducing expected new franchise openings to 22-26 and emphasizing that comp trends should improve in the second half, with Q4 higher than Q3, as refranchising finalizes through lease assignments and the new operating model becomes visible in the back half of 2026.

data.title: QuidelOrtho forecasts $2.52B-$2.60B 2026 revenue amid China pricing uncertainty and withdraws free cash flow guidance
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: QuidelOrtho (QDEL) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "While we are navigating significant headwinds in China and a softer respiratory environment, the underlying performance of our business remains strong." (President, CEO & Director Brian Blaser)

  • "Total revenue in the quarter increased 2%." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) He added that "excluding China, revenue grew 6%" and highlighted demand outside China, including "Labs revenue outside of China grew 9%, Immunohematology revenue outside of China increased 5%, and Triage expanded by 9%." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • "Adjusted EBITDA increased 21% to $129 million, while EBITDA margin expanded 310 basis points to 20% of revenue." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) He said the margin performance "demonstrates that our operational improvement initiatives are delivering tangible results." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • "One of the most significant of these opportunities is the commercialization of the LEX point of care molecular platform, now branded as NULEXA." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) He said, "we remain on track" and expects "customer placements and test utilization to gain steady momentum as we progress into the respiratory season later this year." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • "China, where revenue declined 23% year-over-year." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) He linked the decline to policy uncertainty: "Uncertainty related to the proposed IVD pricing guidelines has impacted buying behavior as customers reduce their inventories pending the issuance of the final nationwide guidelines." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • "We made the decision to withdraw free cash flow guidance until we have greater clarity of the combined working capital implications of these developments." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • "QuidelOrtho has a highly attractive global diagnostics franchise, a large installed base, and leading market positions." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Micah Young) He added, "I see clear opportunities to improve execution and strengthen cash conversion." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

Outlook

  • "We now expect revenue in the range of $2.52 billion to $2.60 billion." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He said the revision reflects: "we expect the challenges in China to persist" and "we are taking a prudent approach to respiratory season assumptions in the second half." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "We are assuming approximately 3% to 5% aggregate growth for those businesses in the second half of the year." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He specified the assumption applies to "our core laboratory and Immunohematology businesses outside of China." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "We now expect full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $540 million to $560 million, representing an EBITDA margin range of 21% to 22%." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He also guided, "we now expect adjusted EPS of $0.65 to $0.90." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "We made the decision to withdraw free cash flow guidance." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He said the withdrawal reflects uncertainty tied to "the current market environment in China" and "the ultimate strength and timing of the respiratory season, and the related working capital impacts." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

Financial Results

  • "Total revenue for the quarter was $631 million." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He noted mix and geography: "Revenue outside of China, which represents nearly 90% of total company revenue, increased 6% year-over-year in Q2." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "Q2 adjusted gross margin was 44.4%, down 130 basis points year-over-year." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He attributed pressure to "the unfavorable geographic mix associated with lower China volumes." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "Operating cash flow for the quarter was negative $111 million, and free cash flow is negative $136 million." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He cited one-time and strategic items including: "Second quarter free cash flow included a $25 million payment to Grifols" and "we deployed $97 million in cash for the LEX acquisition." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • "At the end of the second quarter, net debt leverage was 4.3x adjusted EBITDA." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young) He said priorities include "improving cash conversion and reducing leverage." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

Q&A

  • Jack Meehan, Operon Research, LLC: "what proactive steps you're taking to improve the balance sheet leverage." Chief Financial Officer Young: "improving working capital, reducing the capital that's tied up into inventory, optimizing the returns on our instrument investments, rationalizing capital expenditures, and directing capital towards the geographies and businesses generating the highest returns."

  • Jack Meehan, Operon Research, LLC: asked about an article "reporting that QuidelOrtho was considering selling its point of care business." President, CEO & Director Blaser: "I'm not going to comment on that" and "we don't comment on market rumors like that," while adding that "our board and our management team are regularly evaluating a broad range of opportunities, including portfolio opportunities."

  • Jack Meehan, Operon Research, LLC: asked for color on the reduced respiratory forecast and whether it was "Australia data or something else." President, CEO & Director Blaser: "our approach to forecasting for it" has shifted and "we are assuming that the respiratory testing market is going to be consistent with more of the lower end of the historical seasons," citing "lower strength of data coming out of the Southern Hemisphere."

  • William Bonello, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, Research Division: questioned how the company mitigates underperformance in parts of the business. President, CEO & Director Blaser: "When you step back and look at the business excluding respiratory and China... Those are really strong, predictable businesses" and "we are taking very aggressive mitigation steps in China and across the business" including "a lot of cost improvement opportunities underway."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to skeptical, emphasizing concentration risk and durability of growth, including the framing that "if you don't count something that's not growing, then growth looks pretty good." (William Bonello, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, Research Division)

  • Management tone was slightly defensive on rumors and more cautious on near-term demand, including "I'm not going to comment on that" (President, CEO & Director Blaser) and "we do not have sufficient clarity today" to provide free cash flow guidance. (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • Versus Q1, management language shifted from expecting normalization to modeling continued softness; in Q1, the company said it was "continuing to plan for an average respiratory season" (Chief Financial Officer Joseph Busky) while in Q2 it said, "we are assuming the first-half softness continues" and "have modeled our second-half respiratory revenues accordingly." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Management changes were a central update in Q2: "I'd like to welcome Micah Young, our new Chief Financial Officer." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) In Q1, Joseph Busky served as CFO and delivered guidance. (Chief Financial Officer Joseph Busky)

  • Guidance moved lower in Q2 versus Q1: Q1 guided "total reported revenue of $2.7 billion to $2.75 billion" and "adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.80 to $2.00" (Chief Financial Officer Busky), while Q2 guided "revenue in the range of $2.52 billion to $2.60 billion" and "adjusted EPS of $0.65 to $0.90." (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

  • Free cash flow stance tightened: Q1 said, "we expect to deliver free cash flow of $100 million to $120 million" (Chief Financial Officer Busky), while Q2 said, "we made the decision to withdraw free cash flow guidance." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • China commentary shifted from timing confidence to faster-than-expected demand disruption; in Q1, management said, "We don't think the changes will be fully implemented until the middle of next year" (President, CEO & Director Blaser), while in Q2 it said customers adjusted "more quickly and significantly than we had anticipated." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

Risks and Concerns

  • China demand risk centered on policy uncertainty: "the timing, extent, and pace of implementation continue to create uncertainty around near-term demand." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) Mitigation was described as "protecting our installed base" and "aligning commercial resources with the evolving reimbursement environment." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • Respiratory variability was positioned as a key swing factor: "early indicators are pointing to a below-average season ahead." (President, CEO & Director Blaser) Management said it intends to "take a more conservative approach and align our cost structure accordingly." (President, CEO & Director Blaser)

  • Cash generation and leverage were highlighted as near-term constraints, with Q2 cash usage and leverage acknowledged alongside actions to respond: "Improving cash conversion, reducing leverage, and maintaining a disciplined capital allocation framework" were stated priorities. (Chief Financial Officer & Principal Financial Officer Young)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q2 as a quarter where revenue growth and margin expansion outside China were offset by a sharper China decline and a softer respiratory backdrop, prompting a full-year reset to $2.52B-$2.60B of revenue, $540M-$560M of adjusted EBITDA, and $0.65-$0.90 of adjusted EPS. Leadership emphasized intensified focus on cost structure, cash conversion, and deleveraging, while withdrawing free cash flow guidance until working-capital impacts from China policy uncertainty and respiratory season timing become clearer, alongside continued execution on the NULEXA commercialization plan.

data.title: Consumers' medium- and long-term inflation expectations appear anchored: NY Fed
data.description:
Consumers' outlook for inflation expectations hasn't changed much in the past month, but they still don't see inflation falling to the Federal Reserve's 2% goal anytime soon, according to the New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations.

Their outlook on their current and future household financial situation looked a little brighter. Meanwhile, their expectations on job loss deteriorated, while their perception of finding a job if they needed to improved. 

The median inflation expectation at the one-year-ahead timeframe ticked down 0.1 percentage point to 3.6% in July, while those at the three-year and five-year horizons were unchanged at 3.3% and 3.0%, respectively.

Consumers also appeared more certain about their inflation expectations at the one- and five-year horizons. The median inflation uncertainty at the three-year horizon was unchanged.

Federal Reserve policymakers closely watch inflation expectations in calculating interest rate decisions. If consumers expect inflation to surge in coming years, the policymakers will be more likely to raise rates to tamp down on demand, thereby reducing inflationary pressures.

The mean perceived probability of losing one's job edged up by 0.1 pp to 14.2%, still below the 12-month trailing average of 14.5%. The mean probability that the U.S. employment rate will rise in the year ahead increased by 1.1 pp to 42.8%.

Consumers' confidence in finding a job if they lose their current one, though, rose, with the mean perceived probability of finding a job up 1.3 pp to 46.2%.

On the household finance side, consumers' median expected growth in household income was unchanged at 3.0% in July. The median year-ahead outlook on spending growth ticked down 0.1 pp to 4.9%, slightly below the 12-month trailing average of 5.0%, the New York Fed said.

Still, they appear to be more concerned about keeping up on debt payments.  The median perceived probability of missing a minimum debt payment over the next three months rose 1.2 pp to 12.0%, still below the 12-month trailing average of 12.7%.

data.title: Medical devices ETF nears breakout; here are its top holdings
data.description:
The U.S. Medical Devices ETF (IHI) could be nearing a technical breakout as strength in the broader healthcare sector prompts investors to rotate into lagging industry groups, according to Donovan Jackson of Stock Market Media.

Jackson said medical devices had been one of the weakest areas within healthcare but could also emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries if artificial intelligence is successfully integrated across the industry.

With the broader healthcare ETF (XLV) on track to end the week at a record high, Jackson said capital could gradually rotate into underperforming healthcare subsectors rather than continue chasing stocks that had already posted strong gains.

A chart shared by Jackson showed IHI forming what he described as a tactical base just below its pivot lows from April. According to the analysis, a move above the $55 level would mark a breakout and open the door for a rally toward the next resistance area near $65, implying a potential upside of nearly 20%.

Jackson said the setup offered investors an opportunity to gain exposure to the healthcare sector without chasing recent winners.
